==English==

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈt͡ʃiːt/|[ˈt͡ʃʰɪi̯t]}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-cheat.ogg|a=US}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-cheat.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{rhymes|en|iːt|s=1}}
* {{hyph|en|cheat}}

===Etymology 1===
{{ety|en|id=violate|:inh|enm:escheten<alt:achetan>|enm:achete<alt:chete>|tree=1}}
Verb from {{der|en|enm|achetan}}, variant of {{m|enm|escheten}}, from {{der|en|fro|escheat}}, past participle of {{m|fro|escheoir}}, {{m|fro|escheoiter}}, from {{der|en|LL.|*excadēre||fall away, fall out}}, from {{prefix|la|l=Latin|ex-|cadō|alt2=cadere|t2=fall|nocat=1}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|beswīcan}}.

Noun from verb and/or {{der|en|enm|chete}}, aphetic form of {{m|enm|achete}}, {{m|enm|escheat}}, {{m|enm|eschete||the reversion of property to the state}}, from {{der|en|xno|eschete}} and {{der|en|fro|eschet}}, {{m|fro|escheit}}, {{m|fro|escheoit||that which falls to one}}, past participle of {{m|fro|escheoir||to fall}} (modern {{cog|fr|échoir}}), from {{der|en|LL.|*excadēre||fall away, fall out}}, from {{prefix|la|l=Latin|ex-|cadō|alt2=cadere|t2=fall|nocat=1}}.

{{doublet|en|escheat}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[violate]] rules in order to gain, or attempt to gain, advantage from a situation.
#: {{ux|en|My brother flunked biology because he '''cheated''' on his mid-term.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To be [[unfaithful]] to one's [[spouse]] or [[partner]]; to commit [[adultery]], or to engage in sexual or romantic conduct with a person other than one's partner in contravention of the rules of society or agreement in the relationship.
#: {{syn|en|[[step out on someone|step out on]]}}
#: {{ux|en|My husband '''cheated''' on me with his secretary.}}
#: {{ux|en|After he found out his wife '''cheated''', he left her.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2003|author=Martin Kantor|title=Distancing: Avoidant Personality Disorder|page=137
|passage=While the nonavoidant passive-aggressive '''cheats''' for the sexual gratification and tries to disguise his or her '''cheating''' afterwards, in contrast, the passive-aggressive avoidant '''cheats''' less for the sex than to send a message{{...}}}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[avoid]] a seemingly inevitable thing.
#: {{ux|en|He '''cheated''' death when his car collided with a moving train.}}
#: {{ux|en|I feel as if I've '''cheated''' fate.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[deceive]]; to [[fool]]; to [[trick]].
#: {{syn|en|rook|blench|lirt|burn|q4=informal, usually passive|beguile|q5=literary}}
#: {{ux|en|My ex-wife '''cheated''' me out of $40,000.}}
#: {{ux|en|He '''cheated''' his way into office.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Tempest|act=III|scene=ii|passage=I am subject to a tyrant, a sorcerer, that by his cunning hath '''cheated''' me of this island.}}
#* {{RQ:Irving Sketch Book|title=Rural Life in England|page=130|passage=[T]he holly providentially planted about the house, to '''cheat''' winter of its dreariness, and throw in a gleam of green summer to cheer the fireside:—all these bespeak the influence of taste, flowing down from high sources, and pervading the lowest levels of the public mind.}}
# {{lb|en|informal|intransitive}} To disregard self-imposed restrictions or commitments in favour of resting or indulging oneself.

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|countable}} An act of deception or fraud; that which is the means of fraud or deception.
#: {{syn|en|fraud|trick|imposition|imposture}}
#* {{RQ:Dryden Aureng-zebe|passage=When I consider life, 'tis all a '''cheat'''.}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} Someone who cheats.
#: {{syn|en|cheater|q1=informal|bandit}}
#* {{RQ:Eddison Worm|page=33|passage=And he smote Corinius on his shaven jowl with the dice box, calling him '''cheat''' and mangy rascal, whereupon Corinius drew forth a bodkin to smite him in the neck withal; but some went betwixt them, and with much ado and much struggling and cursing they were parted, and it being shown that the dice were not loaded, the son of Corund was fain to make amends to Corinius, and so were they set at one again.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=4 Feb 90|volume=17|number=29|journal=Gay Community News|page=13|author=Margy Dowzer;Mary Frances Platt;Aviva Shmuckler|title=Disability And Accessibility Cost Money!|text=The caseworker couldn't understand how I could have stretched out my last bit of money for so long. She seemed convinced that I was "hiding" income from her and interrogated me for I don't know how long {{...}} The system seems based on the assumption that people are "welfare '''cheats'''. If you don't speak English or are marginal in some other way, it's worse. I wish they'd put the Defense Department through what we go through.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} The weed [[cheatgrass]].
# {{senseid|en|Q1004599}} {{lb|en|card games|uncountable}} {{syn of|en|bullshit<id:Q1004599>||a card game where the goal is to have no cards remaining in a hand, often by telling [[lies]]}}.
# {{lb|en|video games|countable}} A hidden means of gaining an unfair advantage in a [[video game]], often by entering a [[cheat code]].
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1992|author=Phil Howard|title=Cheat Mode|journal=Amstrad Action|issue=76|month=January|page=32
|passage=I've had a number of requests for a '''cheat''' for Turrican the first. Yes, there is a keypress built in {{...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1998|title=GamePro Issue 109 August 1998|page=141
|passage=Unpause the game, then repause the game and enter any of the following '''cheats''': {{...}}}}

===Etymology 2===
{{ety|en|id=bread|:inh|enm:chet}}
{{inh+|en|enm|chet|t=low-quality bread}}, of unknown origin; compare {{m|en|manchet}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun|-}}

# {{lb|en|obsolete}} A [[sort]] of low-quality [[bread]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1587|volume=I|author=[[w:Raphael Holinshed|Raphaell Holinshed]]; Iohn Hooker|chapter=Of the food and diet of the Engliſh|title=[[w:Holinshed's Chronicles|The firſt and ſecond volumes of Chronicles{{...}}]]|page=169|location=London|publisher=Henry Denham|passage=The raueled '''cheat''' therfore is generallie ſo made that out of one buſhell of meale, after two and twentie pounds of bran be ſifted and taken from it (wherevnto they ad the [[gurgeons]] that riſe from the manchet) they make thirtie cast, euerie lofe weighing eightéene ounces into the ouen and ſixteene ounces out{{...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=c.1624|author=w:Homer|translator=w:George Chapman|title=[[w:Batrachomyomachia|The crowne of all Homers workes Batrachomyomachia]]{{...}}|publisher=Iohn Bill|url=https://quod.lib.umich.edu/e/eebo/A03505.0001.001?view=toc|passage=Takes part with them, at ſhore: their pureſt '''cheat''', / Thrice boulted, kneaded, and ſubdu'd in paſt{{...}}|page=3}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1746|author=Thomas Moffett; Christopher Bennet|title=Health's Improvement{{...}}|publisher=T. Oſborne|location=London|page=339|url=https://www.google.co.nz/books/edition/Health_s_Improvement_Or_Rules_Comprizing|passage=Where by the way note, that loaves made of pure Wheaten Meal require both more Leaven and more labouring, and more baking than either coarſe '''Cheat''' or than Bread Mingled of Meal and Grudgins.}}
